notes.W7225792625: First phase 3 evidence that a personalised neoantigen mRNA therapy adds to checkpoint blockade: 24-month recurrence-free survival 82.2% vs 70.0% in 1,137 patients. The benefit only appears after six months (HR 0.42), consistent with time needed to raise new T cells. Follow-up is still short for overall survival.
notes.W7147157634: Small, incremental models trained only on one child's home recordings learned phoneme- and word-like units at that child's own pace. Learning needed dense daily input plus replay of recent experience. A direct test of how much structure everyday speech carries, though with only eight children.
notes.W7225465743: A clean, large null: in 6,376 high-risk patients, ziltivekimab cut free IL-6 by 76 points and CRP by 64, yet MACE was identical (HR 0.99). Lowering the inflammatory marker did not lower events, a sharp challenge to IL-6 as a causal cardiovascular target.
notes.W4417295272: Settles how many uses of an unknown quantum process are needed to learn it to fixed diamond-distance accuracy, with matching upper and lower bounds. The trick reduces channel learning to pure-state tomography via the Choi state, so states, unitaries and measurements fall under one framework.
notes.W4416048293: Completes a rigorous proof of the 1957 Huang–Yang formula for the dilute repulsive Fermi gas energy to third order, by adding the matching lower bound. The result confirms that only the scattering length matters at this order, a universality physicists have long assumed.
notes.W4408079350: Genomes from 4,587 ancient Europeans test rival homelands for Celtic. Three migrations fit; the authors favour a Late Bronze Age westward spread from eastern central Europe. A model of using genetics to bound linguistic history, with the honest caveat that language shifts need not follow genes.
notes.W4390843425: Natural experiments in Florida show fragile, under-capitalised insurers causally raise mortgage defaults after disasters, and that GSEs accept them without pricing the risk. Lenders screen insurer quality only on loans they keep, so roughly a quarter of GSE expected losses there trace to insurance fragility.
notes.W7203849053: Older adults (70–80) accessed word meanings faster than young adults across three studies, traced to changed conceptual representations and reproduced by learning simulations. The advantage reverses when learned knowledge conflicts with the task, reframing some 'slowing' as accumulated learning rather than decline.
notes.W4413345846: Saturation editing scored 4,113 new BRCA1 variants; HAP1 scores separate pathogenic from benign almost perfectly. But nearly half of HAP1 loss-of-function variants looked neutral in mammary epithelial cells, and these turn out to be hypomorphs with intermediate cancer risk. Cell context changes variant interpretation.
notes.W4410357547: A multi-region single-cell and spatial atlas of 12 glioblastomas finds that cancer cell diversity follows one stereotyped path, from developmental-like states toward injury-response and hypoxic states, repeated across tumours and genetic subclones. Heterogeneity becomes a trajectory tied to myeloid niches, not a random mixture.

thread: The BRCA1 and glioblastoma papers make the same point from opposite ends: genotype does not fix phenotype. The same BRCA1 variant is damaging in one cell type and neutral in another, while genetically different glioblastoma subclones converge on the same state trajectory dictated by their tissue niche. In both, context is a variable you must measure, not noise to average away.

notes.W4417295272: Shifts: learning quantum processes treated as a separate, harder problem with unknown optimal cost → channel tomography reduces exactly to pure-state tomography with proven optimal query complexity. Process learning now sits on the same footing as state learning, unifying states, unitaries and measurements.
notes.W4416048293: Shifts: the Huang–Yang third-order energy of the dilute Fermi gas was a 1957 physical prediction → it is a theorem, universal across interaction potentials. Universality via the scattering length is now proven, not assumed, at this order for fermions.
notes.W7225984440: Shifts: whether a nonenzymatic phosphoryl transfer beats hydrolysis was case-by-case → one linear free-energy scale predicts rates across 14 orders of magnitude. It explains why imidazole, hence histidine, is the optimal catalyst for ATP-like donors.
notes.W7165116167: Shifts: pulsars and magnetars implied two distinct initial field populations → a single log-uniform distribution suffices, with the gap produced by faster inclination alignment (τ ∝ B⁻²) reducing beaming of high-field stars. Two classes become one population seen through a selection effect.

foundation.title: Behaviour reflects accumulated input, not fixed capacity
foundation.principle: How a mind performs is largely a readout of the statistics it has absorbed, so changes in performance often reflect what was learned rather than how much machinery is available. The child-specific models show that phonemes and words can emerge from one child's ordinary speech stream, with learning pace tracking the density of input and replay, no innate grammar module needed. The ageing study is the same principle at the far end of life: decades of language exposure reshape conceptual representations, making older adults faster when a task matches that knowledge and slower when it conflicts. The principle applies wherever learners are judged: test scores across cultures, expertise effects, and AI models evaluated outside their training distribution.
rests_on: Saffran, Aslin & Newport (1996). Statistical learning by 8-month-old infants
foundation.question: How much of what we call cognitive decline would disappear if tasks were matched to each person's lifetime input statistics?

W7225792625.question: Does adding a personalised neoantigen therapy to adjuvant pembrolizumab reduce melanoma recurrence after surgery?
W7225792625.approach: Phase 3 double-blind RCT, 1,137 patients with resected stage IIB–IV melanoma, randomised 2:1 to intismeran or placebo, both with pembrolizumab.
W7225792625.finding: 24-month RFS 82.2% vs 70.0%; distant-metastasis-free 88.5% vs 80.2%. HR 0.42 after six months, none before. Grade ≥3 AEs 23.6% vs 20.3%.
W7225792625.implication: Individualised cancer vaccines now have randomised phase 3 support as an add-on to checkpoint inhibitors, with delayed onset of benefit.

W7147157634.question: Is a single child's everyday speech input enough to learn language units without built-in linguistic knowledge?
W7147157634.approach: Trained cognitively feasible models incrementally on longitudinal home recordings from eight children across their first 1,000 days.
W7147157634.finding: Models developed phoneme-like and word-form representations tracking each child's pace; learning required dense daily sampling and replay of recent input.
W7147157634.implication: Everyday input carries enough structure for early language; child-specific models become a tool for testing developmental theories.

W7225465743.question: Does neutralising interleukin-6 reduce cardiovascular events in inflamed patients with atherosclerosis and chronic kidney disease?
W7225465743.approach: Multinational double-blind RCT of 6,376 patients with CRP ≥2 mg/L, monthly ziltivekimab 15 mg vs placebo, median 33 months.
W7225465743.finding: IL-6 fell 76 points and CRP 64 points, but MACE occurred in 17.6% vs 17.7% (HR 0.99, P = 0.84).
W7225465743.implication: Suppressing IL-6 and CRP does not prevent events here, weakening IL-6 as a causal target in this population.

W4417295272.question: How many uses of an unknown quantum channel are needed to learn it to fixed accuracy in diamond distance?
W4417295272.approach: Prepare Choi-state copies, purify them, apply optimal pure-state tomography, then project onto valid channels; prove a matching lower bound.
W4417295272.finding: Optimal query complexity established, with tight dependence on input and output dimensions and Kraus rank at constant accuracy.
W4417295272.implication: Process tomography reduces to pure-state tomography, giving one optimal framework for states, unitaries, measurements and channels.

W4416048293.question: Is the 1957 Huang–Yang three-term formula for the dilute Fermi gas ground-state energy mathematically correct?
W4416048293.approach: Rigorous analysis of spin-1/2 fermions with repulsive short-range interactions, proving a lower bound to match the authors' earlier upper bound.
W4416048293.finding: The three-term asymptotic expansion holds, depending on the potential only through its scattering length.
W4416048293.implication: A foundational many-body prediction is now a theorem, confirming universality in dilute quantum gases at this order.

W4408079350.question: Which proposed homeland and route best explains the Iron Age spread of Celtic languages across Europe?
W4408079350.approach: Genome-wide analysis of 4,587 ancient individuals, mainly Bronze and Iron Age Europe, tested against archaeological and linguistic models.
W4408079350.finding: Three movements: Bell Beaker Steppe ancestry after ~4400 BP, southwest Europe to Britain 3800–3200 BP, eastern central Europe westward 3200–2800 BP.
W4408079350.implication: The eastern central European expansion is most parsimonious for Celtic, narrowing the plausible scenarios for its emergence.

W4390843425.question: How does mispriced climate and insurer risk flow into mortgage markets and taxpayer exposure?
W4390843425.approach: New combined mortgage and insurance dataset for Florida 2009–2018, using multiple natural experiments around disasters and insurer insolvencies.
W4390843425.finding: Insurer insolvency causally raises post-disaster defaults; about 25% of GSE expected Florida losses stem from insurance fragility; lenders screen only retained jumbo loans.
W4390843425.implication: GSE reliance on third-party insurer ratings subsidises credit to risky areas; fixing insurer evaluation would reprice climate risk.

W7203849053.question: Is slower responding in old age always decline, or can lifelong learning make older adults faster?
W7203849053.approach: Three studies comparing adults aged 70–80 and 18–25 on semantic tasks, semantic ratings, and learning simulations of cumulative language experience.
W7203849053.finding: Older adults were faster at accessing word meanings, explained by changed conceptual representations; the advantage shrank when learned information conflicted with task demands.
W7203849053.implication: Cognitive ageing frameworks centred on decline and compensation miss benefits that arise from accumulated representational learning.

W4413345846.question: Can saturation genome editing resolve uncertain BRCA1 variants, and do variant effects hold across cell types?
W4413345846.approach: SGE of 11 BRCA1 regions in HAP1 cells scoring 4,113 new variants, plus a new SGE assay in mammary epithelial cells.
W4413345846.finding: 538 function-impacting variants; near-perfect pathogenic/benign separation in HAP1; nearly half of HAP1 loss-of-function variants were neutral in HMECs.
W4413345846.implication: Discordant variants are hypomorphs with intermediate cancer risk, so multi-cell-type assays sharpen clinical variant interpretation.

W4410357547.question: Do glioblastoma's diverse cancer cell states arise randomly or follow a defined trajectory across tumours?
W4410357547.approach: Single-cell and spatial multi-omic atlas of 12 tumours across regions, deep-learning mapping of states and clones in situ, organoid validation.
W4410357547.finding: Cells move from developmental-like toward injury-response and hypoxic states, conserved across tumours and subclones, with subclones finely intermixed spatially.
W4410357547.implication: Glioblastoma heterogeneity becomes a tractable trajectory linked to myeloid signalling niches, suggesting state-directed rather than clone-directed targets.

figure_notes.W4417295272: Read the figure left to right as a pipeline. The unknown channel acts on halves of maximally entangled pairs, producing copies of its Choi state. A purification step turns these into pure states, which an optimal pure-state tomography learns. A final semidefinite program projects the estimate onto physically valid channels, guaranteeing diamond-distance error below ε.
figure_notes.W4408079350: Panel a is the map: circled regions are the four candidate Celtic homelands, and shading shows where Celtic was spoken around 2,000 years ago. Panel b is a schematic language tree placing Proto-Celtic between its split from other Indo-European branches and its later divergence into Brittonic and Goidelic. Branch lengths are illustrative only.
figure_notes.W4413345846: Panel a shows the design: 11 BRCA1 regions edited in HAP1 cells with a library of every possible single-nucleotide change, then sequenced at days 5 and 14 to see which variants drop out. Panel b plots function scores by mutation type for 3,843 variants; low scores mean the variant impairs cell fitness, flagging loss of function.
figure_notes.W4410357547: Panel a outlines the study design. Panel b is the atlas overview: a UMAP where each point is a nucleus, clustered into malignant (657,275) and microenvironment (368,054) cells, with a ring plot showing composition at three levels of detail. Panel c clusters malignant states by transcriptome, the basis for the trajectory.
